title: Three-step pilot escape hatch play
content:
Deck purpose: short, repeatable three-step sequence SEs and field ops can run when a pilot starts to stall or shows early signs of failing. Goal = prevent churn, preserve credibility, salvage momentum, and create a safe pause with quick restart paths.

Slide 1 – Title: Three-step Pilot Escape Hatch
- One-liner: When a pilot derails, run these three steps in <48h to de-risk and re-align.
- Who uses: SE, Solutions Eng, Customer Success, Platform Ops.

Slide 2 – Why this exists (context)
- Observed failure modes: throughput/latency surprises, cost delta vs. expectations, data access delays, unexpected model hallucinations, procurement/legal hold, infra throttles.
- Typical consequences: pilot paused, PO loses confidence, pilot never resumes.
- Hypothesis: a short, prescriptive play reduces friction and gives a clear restart path.

Slide 3 – High-level three steps (the play)
1) Pause + communicate (safe pause)
2) Triage + temporary downgrade (fast fallback)
3) Restart path + success gating (clear restart checklist)
- Timing: aim to complete steps 1 & 2 within 24–48 hours.

Slide 4 – Step 1: Pause + communicate (concrete)
- When: visible signs of scope creep, SLA miss, legal/procurement blockers, or unhappy stakeholder.
- Action items (SE):
  • Immediately send a 1-paragraph status to primary stakeholders and internal pilot-ops channel (template below).
  • Propose a short pause window (48–72h) to triage — framing: "temporary safety hold to avoid bigger rework".
  • Set expectations: we will not change core scope during triage; no new feature asks.
- Templates:
  Slack DM to customer PM: "We’re seeing X (latency/cost/drift). We recommend a 48h safety pause so we can triage and return with a clear fix plan. Will that work for you?"
  Internal Slack: "Pilot [acct] pausing for 48h. Triage leads = Priya/Miguel. Blocking signals = latency>800ms / cost>3x estimate / model errors>5%."

Slide 5 – Step 2: Triage + temporary downgrade (playbook)
- Triage checklist (quick):
  1) Metrics snapshot: last 7d latency P95, cost per 1k tokens, error rate on sample prompts (QA harness), throughput vs required QPS. (Owner: SE/Solutions)
  2) Configs: batching, prefix cache settings, seq length caps, quantization profile used. (Owner: Infra/SRE)
  3) Model: model family + quantization variant + fallback options available. (Owner: Research/Model Ops)
  4) Network/Access: are any VPC/KMS/proxy calls blocked? (Owner: CS/Customer IT)
- Fast fallback options (pick one):
  • Route traffic to a lower-cost but compatible model variant (quantized or smaller family) for the pilot window.
  • Reduce max tokens / enforce stricter stop tokens and input truncation.
  • Enable prefix/KV caching aggressively for repeat queries.
- Risk note: fast fallbacks may slightly degrade quality. Communicate tradeoff explicitly.

Slide 6 – Example quick fallback recipe
- Problem: Latency spikes from long context + bursty QPS.
- Recipe:
  1) Enforce 2s client timeout, cap seq_length to 1024, enable prefix cache for repetitive prompts.
  2) Route 100% pilot traffic to model-x-8q (verified compat) during 48h window.
  3) Add traffic sampling: keep 5% routed to original model for quality checks.
- Owner: SE + SRE + Research.

Slide 7 – Step 3: Restart path + success gating
- Re-start checklist (must be green to resume):
  • Latency P95 below agreed threshold for 24h under pilot load.
  • Cost per 1k tokens within 20% of target estimate or business agrees to delta.
  • Quality score on templated eval > baseline (we'll use the pilot prompt set).
  • Legal/procurement items removed or on committed timeline with owner.
- Restart communication: escalate to exec sponsor, propose phased re-enable (25% -> 50% -> 100%).

Slide 8 – SE cheat snippets (copy-paste)
- Pause message (email):
  Subject: Pilot temporary hold — [Account] — [Reason]
  Body: Quick note: based on initial runs we’re hitting [latency/cost/quality]. We propose a 48h hold while we execute a targeted triage and fallback to avoid rework. We’ll share results and a clear restart plan within 48 hours.
- Internal triage kickoff (Slack):
  "Triage kickoff for [acct] — issue: high P95 latency. Owners: @miguel @ava @tom. First pass: metrics snapshot (Miguel), config check (Tom), model eval (Ava). ETA 24h."

Slide 9 – Common objections & suggested responses
- Objection: "We can’t pause — we need continuous delivery."
  Response: "Short pause reduces risk of repeated failures and costly rework; propose a narrow 48h window and phased resume."
- Objection: "Fallback will hurt quality."
  Response: "We’ll gate quality with a 5% sample against baseline and keep a plan to revert. The temporary change avoids bigger outages while we triage."

Slide 10 – Signals to escalate immediately
- Data exfil concerns, PII/KMS errors, legal hold, major hallucination causing safety/regulatory risk.
- Escalation path: SE -> CS -> Legal/Security + Exec sponsor. Use emergency channel: #pilot-ops-critical.

Slide 11 – Measurement & templates
- Quick metrics dashboard (what to pull): P95 latency, average tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens, success rate on eval prompts, 24h active user count.
- SQL snippets and dashboard ids (placeholder): CONF-PLT-dashboard, Jira INF-4272 (triage board).

Slide 12 – Open questions / TO DOs (work-in-progress)
- Need a small canned set of model-variant compatibility matrices (Research).
- Product: can we expose a 2-click pilot pause in Console? (low priority but high value).
- Legal: suggested wording for "temporary pause" for procurement docs (Tom to draft).
- Engineering: sample automated rollback play (GitHub PR exists but needs review: /pull/452).

Slide 13 – Next steps & owners
- Today: send pause template (SE) + create triage ticket INF-4272 (SE) — owner: Priya.
- 24h: metrics snapshot + fallback selected (Miguel).
- 48h: run restart gating checks; if green, execute phased resume (CS + SE).

Appendix (quick references)
- Sample prompt set to run evals: 30 canonical pilot prompts (see Confluence CONF-PLT-escape-hatch).
- Contact list: Priya Natarajan (PMM), Miguel Santos (SE lead), Ava Chen (Research), Tom Bauer (Legal).
- Slack snippets, email templates, and a minimal SQL query for P95 included in the Confluence draft.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this <2 pages in final; field folks want a one-pager + 30s elevator pitch.
- Consider adding a one-click Console action in Q1 roadmap — flag to Product.
- Validate fallback model quality with 3 customers before socializing widely.

Unresolved: who owns the official "pilot pause" audit trail for compliance (Legal vs CS)? Put on next week's PM sync.
